guide_btn_tip: Step-by-step setup guide: Synapse, drivers, first combo.
guide_p1_body:
Your Wolverine has extra buttons (**M1–M6**), but a game can only see them as ordinary buttons or keyboard keys.

This app catches each **M-button** the moment you press it, hides it from the game, and sends a **combo** on a **virtual Xbox controller** instead: for example **RB + A**, a **hold-then-press**, a full **macro**, or rapid fire.

Because the game only ever sees controller input, it stays in **controller mode**: no keyboard prompts, no flickering interface.

This guide takes about two minutes. You can reopen it any time with the **? GUIDE** button at the top of the window.
guide_p2_body:
Use the dropdown at the **top left** of the window.

•  **WOLVERINE V3 PRO 8K (PC)** — Synapse can make the M-buttons send **keyboard keys**. This is the simplest setup: follow Step 2.

•  **WOLVERINE V2 / V2 CHROMA / V2 PRO** — Razer's software can only make the paddles copy **normal pad buttons**, so each M-button has to **sacrifice** one real button. Follow Step 3 instead.

The choice is saved with your profile.
guide_p3_body:
1.  Open **Razer Synapse** and select your **Wolverine V3 Pro 8K**.
2.  Open the **Customize** tab and click a paddle, for example **M1**.
3.  Choose **Keyboard Function** — not a controller button.
4.  Pick a key you never use while playing. We recommend one default per paddle:
     **M1 = Scroll Lock**,  **M2 = Pause**,  **M3 = Insert**,  **M4 = Home**,  **M5 = Page Up**,  **M6 = Page Down**.
5.  Repeat for every paddle, then make sure the profile is **saved to the controller** so it keeps working when Synapse is not in front.

Prefer other keys? No problem: in this app click **REBIND KEY** on the M-button and press the key you chose. The app simply uses whatever key arrives.
guide_p4_body:
Skip this page if you have a V3 Pro 8K.

1.  In **Razer Controller Setup for Xbox**, map each paddle to a pad button you can spare, for example **View**, **Menu**, **LS click** or **RS click**.
2.  In this app, select the M-button and pick the same button under **SACRIFICED BUTTON**. That button is now the trigger and no longer works as itself in games.
3.  Turn **Passthrough** on in the profile bar. The app then mirrors your whole pad into the virtual controller, with the sacrificed buttons removed.
4.  Install **HidHide** (Settings tab → DRIVERS) and hide the physical Wolverine, so the game only sees the **virtual controller**.
guide_p5_body:
The virtual controller is created by the **ViGEmBus** driver. The installer sets it up, and the **Settings** tab shows whether it is installed.

Press **START ENGINE** at the top right. The badge turns **ENGINE ONLINE**, the virtual controller appears, and your M-buttons are now intercepted.

While the engine is **stopped**, the M-buttons type real keys into Windows and games — that is what flips a game to keyboard mode. Tip: in **Settings** you can start the engine automatically and start the app with Windows.

Closing the window does **not** quit: the app keeps running in the **tray** at the bottom right. Right-click the tray icon to stop the engine, switch profile, or quit.
guide_p6_body:
Click a green **M badge** on the controller picture. The panel on the right opens with two tabs:

•  **MANUAL** — choose the **TRIGGER** (hold / toggle / double-tap), the **REPEAT** (once / multiple times / while held) and the **ACTION TYPE**: a **CHORD** (buttons together), **HOLD + PRESS** (hold a modifier, then press) or a **MACRO** (your own list of steps).

•  **RECORDER** — press **RECORD FROM PAD**, play the combo on your controller, press **STOP**. The steps are written for you.

The **OUTPUT** line at the bottom always shows what the M-button will send. Press **SAVE** in the profile bar to keep it.
guide_p7_body:
Press an M-button on the controller: its badge lights up and the **console** at the bottom logs what was sent.

Launch your game. Anything that works with your real controller works with the virtual one — the combos are simply extra buttons.

If the game switches to **keyboard mode**, either the engine is not running or Synapse sends a different key than the app expects. Check **ENGINE ONLINE** and the key shown next to the M-button.

Have fun! Found a bug or have an idea? The **GitHub** link is in the **Settings** tab.
overlay_intro: A small see-through controller that stays on top of your game and lights up every button, stick and M-button live — a visual cue that your combos are firing.
overlay_lock_tip: Unlocked: drag the overlay with the mouse, right-click it to lock. Locked: the mouse passes straight through to the game; unlock here or from the tray icon.
overlay_fullscreen_note: Works over windowed and borderless-window games. Exclusive-fullscreen games draw over every window, including this overlay — switch the game to borderless if it is hidden.
overlay_hint: drag to move · right-click to lock
